bug_semantics: The backend Controller accepted the form postback `_handler` field verbatim and passed it to `runAjaxHandler()`, unlike the AJAX-header path, which required an `on[A-Z][\w+]*`-shaped handler. `runAjaxHandler()` then treated a supplied name matching any controller method as a global handler and invoked it. On the Users controller's permission-free `myaccount` action, a low-privileged authenticated backend user with a valid CSRF token could therefore submit names such as `update_onDelete`, `update_onRestore`, `update_onUnsuspendUser`, or `update_onManualPasswordReset` and reach user-management methods without `backend.manage_users`.
flaw_origin: Commit 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 first added `modules/backend/classes/Controller.php` with the unsafe postback-to-dispatcher data flow at lines 167-170 and the unrestricted method-name fallback at lines 389-395. The framework flaw was later made directly exploitable against the built-in Users controller by 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9, which deliberately set `$requiredPermissions = null` for the self-service action (then named `mysettings`, later `myaccount`). The earlier dispatcher commit is the BIC because it first wrote the root mechanism that accepted an attacker-selected non-AJAX handler name; the permission downgrade exposed that pre-existing mechanism rather than creating it.
ai_marker: absent — the exact BIC commit object identifies author and committer as `Sam Georges <sam@daftspunk.com>` and contains only the message `Welcome to the world, October :-)`; it has no `Co-Authored-By`, `Generated-with`, AI-tool trailer, bot identity, or any other trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/wintercms/winter/security/advisories/GHSA-j5jq-cr68-v2xx describes the asymmetric validation, authenticated/CSRF-required attack, Users-controller permission downgrade, callable user-management methods, affected Composer package `winter/wn-backend-module` <=1.2.12, and patched version 1.2.13.

At v1.2.12, `modules/backend/classes/Controller.php:320-327` reads `post('_handler')` and calls `runAjaxHandler($handler)` without validating the name, while the same file's AJAX path applies the handler-name regular expression. `modules/backend/controllers/Users.php:54-60` clears `$requiredPermissions` when the route action is `myaccount`.

`git log -L '/Execute postback handler/,+12':modules/backend/classes/Controller.php --reverse` traces the unsafe postback block to 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5; `git log --all -S"post('_handler')" -- modules/backend/classes/Controller.php` returns that same commit as the sole exact-string origin. In its tree, `modules/backend/classes/Controller.php:169` forwards the raw field and lines 393-394 call any matching controller method.

Direct-parent verification: `git ls-tree -r d412ea685560a3ce7028346d26fd9a6559eb0827 -- modules/backend/classes/Controller.php modules/backend/controllers/Users.php` produced no entries. Thus the vulnerable Controller path and its vulnerable lines are absent from the immediate parent tree, rather than merely changed or moved there.

The related reachability history is explicit: `git log -S'$this->requiredPermissions = null' -- modules/backend/controllers/Users.php` identifies 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9 as the addition and 7f450741125f8e4d1661c81e9b2219424cf22ece as its removal. The latter creates `modules/backend/controllers/MyAccount.php` and removes the conditional permission downgrade from `modules/backend/controllers/Users.php`.

Direct fix 7c2dbe04ee8d3f3ed668e9ecd167c7f115acf8fd changes `modules/backend/classes/Controller.php`: it adds `validateHandlerName()`, calls it before dispatching a form postback, and reuses it for AJAX. Its direct parent 7f450741125f8e4d1661c81e9b2219424cf22ece still has the raw `_handler` -> `runAjaxHandler($handler)` sequence at lines 321-324, proving this commit is the direct mechanism fix. Additional defense-in-depth in 9aabe55f9092809d5bef70d0529ef9af1a147b78 adds authorization checks in `modules/backend/models/User.php` for save/delete/restore/unsuspend/password-reset operations.

Version cross-check: 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 is contained by tags v1.0.319, v1.1.0, v1.2.0, v1.2.12, and v1.2.13, so it predates every tagged affected major line checked. Fix 7c2dbe04ee8d3f3ed668e9ecd167c7f115acf8fd is absent from v1.2.12 but contained by v1.2.13 and v1.2.14. Tags v1.2.12 and v1.2.13 resolve to b6ac66c5e80ddc9ecd9211c10204cdcee6e14313 and e09c8d3526f3583cb6c3476a021b885088ecd4bd respectively. The first-party release https://github.com/wintercms/winter/releases/tag/v1.2.13 lists closing legacy AJAX postback bypasses, moving My Account, and model-level user-management hardening.

BIC-only attribution check: `git cat-file commit 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5` shows tree e2a7769f40cbe90de296820f0dcd321c90008081, parent d412ea685560a3ce7028346d26fd9a6559eb0827, human author/committer Sam Georges, and no trailers or AI markers. reasoning: The disclosed authorization bypass is a conjunction: the generic postback path accepts method names that the AJAX path rejects, and a reachable controller action must bypass the controller's ordinary permission gate. The first part is the root dispatch flaw and was present from the first addition of Backend Controller in 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5; its direct parent has neither the file nor the lines. Later formatting, response-handling, and CSRF changes preserve the same raw-field data flow, so they are not introducers. Commit 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9 later supplies the built-in Users reachability condition, but does not write the unsafe dispatcher. The remediation mirrors both sides of the conjunction: 7f450741125f8e4d1661c81e9b2219424cf22ece isolates My Account, 7c2dbe04ee8d3f3ed668e9ecd167c7f115acf8fd closes the root handler-name bypass, and later model guards add defense in depth. The direct fix falls between the vulnerable and patched release tags. Finally, the only attribution evidence considered is the 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 commit object, which has ordinary human identity and no AI marker; therefore the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
